title: Multiple stack-based buffer overflow vulnerabilities exist in the boa formIpv6Setup pppoe functionality of Totolink X2000R… (CVE-2026-42020)
description: Multiple stack-based buffer overflow vulnerabilities exist in the boa formIpv6Setup pppoe functionality of the Totolink X2000R device. These vulnerabilities can be triggered by an authenticated HTTP request, specifically targeting the pppoe_dns2 parameter, potentially allowing arbitrary code execution. The affected firmware version is TOTOLINK-X2000R-Gh-V1.0.0-B20250421.1327. The vulnerabilities have a high severity with a CVSS score of 9.1.
aiSummary: The Totolink X2000R device running firmware TOTOLINK-X2000R-Gh-V1.0.0-B20250421.1327 contains multiple stack-based buffer overflow vulnerabilities in the boa web server's formIpv6Setup pppoe functionality. An attacker with authentication privileges can send a specially crafted HTTP request manipulating the pppoe_dns2 parameter to trigger these vulnerabilities, leading to arbitrary code execution. The vulnerabilities are classified under CWE-121 (stack-based buffer overflow) and have a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.1, indicating critical impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation allows an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the affected device, potentially compromising the device's confidentiality, integrity, and availability. This could lead to full control over the device and disruption of network services.
